newsitem.title: CYPRUS: New Cyprus Airways boss next week - source.
newsitem.headline: New Cyprus Airways boss next week - source.

text.p: A new chairman of Cypriot national carrier Cyprus Airways will probably be appointed next week, sources in the airline said on Thursday.

Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters after a cabinet meeting no decision had been taken on a replacement for Vassilis Rologis, who announced his intention to resign two weeks ago.
"We expect an announcement next week," said the airline source, who requested anonymity.
Rologis, chairman since July 1993, tendered his resignation two weeks ago after being elected chairman of the Cypriot Chamber of Commerce and Industry. He remains until his successor is appointed.
The government has an 80 percent stake in Cyprus Airways, while the rest is traded on the Cyprus Stock Exchange. The government appoints nine of the 11 directors, including the chairman.
Reports in newspapers and airline sources have tipped local businessman Charis Loizides as the new chairman.
"He does appear to have a good chance," said the company official. Traders said Loizides has been "very active" as a member of the current board of directors.

"My guess is that the government would want to appoint a chairman from the current board rather than outside the company because many issues have to be tackled," said Theodoulos Charalambides from Laiki Investments, a member of the Popular Bank group.
The government recently deregulated flights from Britain to raise tourist arrivals, which could have an impact on the airline's earnings.
